workflow_pattern: This is a 'F8_automation_with_branches' style workflow. It requires the following operations, in roughly this order: create repository, init multiple branches, add readme with content, add file with exact content, create workflow conditional comment by label, validate automation with test issues. The task should combine these operations into one coherent, realistic request without listing them as separate steps.
question:
Hi! I'm a student working on my CI challenge and I really need help setting up my repository properly. Could you please help me create a new project repository named ci-lint-challenge? I need to initialize it with three branches: main, lint, and format. For the main branch, I need an initial README.md file with the content "# CI Lint Challenge

A repository to test complex GitHub automation and linting workflows." I also need a file named lint_sample.txt with the content "# Lint Sample

This is an example lint sample file." in the lint branch, and a file named format_sample.txt with the content "# Format Sample

This is an example format sample file." in the format branch. I'm really struggling with GitHub automation. Could you help me build a GitHub robot that watches for new issues and comments based on label, but with an extra wrinkle for unlabeled issues? If an issue has a label, use the normal per-label replies: 'lint' label gets "Thanks, our linting reviewers will take a look.", 'format' label gets "Thanks, our formatting reviewers will take a look." But if the issue has NO label at all, don't just send one generic default — first check whether the title contains the word 'urgent': if it does, reply "This is unlabeled but flagged urgent, escalating now."; if it doesn't, reply with the plain default "Thanks for your issue, please add a label so we can route it." After we set up the automation, I need to test it with issues covering all these paths: one labeled 'lint' (title: "Missing semicolon check"), one unlabeled with 'urgent' in the title (title: "urgent: build pipeline broken"), and one unlabeled without it (title: "Question about style guide"). I'm really grateful for any help you can provide!
